entries.name: Bekiut
entries.summary: Free bilingual reader for the Babylonian Talmud and other classical texts, built for readability, with the text split into short lines.
entries.annotation_md:
- Covers all 37 tractates of the Bavli in Hebrew/Aramaic and English, using Sefaria's texts; breaks clauses onto separate lines and suggests well-known passages.
- Formerly called ChavrutAI (chavrutai.com). Despite the old name it is not mainly an AI tool.
- Listed both on Powered by Sefaria and on jewishai.me.
entries.status_note: Disclosure: the author's own project. Checked live 9-Oct-2026.

entries.name: Bavli Kilvavi
entries.summary: Hebrew Talmud reader with Rashi and Tosafot, Steinsaltz, Ein Mishpat and Torah Or panels, variant readings and manuscript images.
entries.annotation_md:
- Hover a sentence for an explanation or for related halakhic rulings; side panels for commentators.
- Texts from the Sefaria API and the Steinsaltz Center. Built by an individual developer.
- Hebrew only.

entries.name: Talmud.page
entries.summary: Simple, fast reader for the Talmud and other texts on phone and desktop.
entries.annotation_md: - Built on Sefaria texts (Powered by Sefaria list).

entries.name: Shitufta
entries.summary: Hebrew Torah text library shown in a traditional page layout.
entries.annotation_md: - Built on Sefaria data (Powered by Sefaria list).

entries.name: Otzaria
entries.summary: Free offline Jewish library app for Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iOS, with fast full-text search across thousands of books.
entries.annotation_md:
- Book data from Sefaria, Dicta, Wikisource, the National Library of Israel and others; users can add their own TXT, DOCX and PDF files.
- Very active development; the code is under a personal-use license, not a standard open-source license.
- The AI agent [Ituria](https://github.com/Sivan22/ituria) was built around it (see the AI section).

entries.name: Talmud Navigator
entries.summary: Per-daf lookup that gathers the biblical verses cited on a page, gives Hebrew word lookup and compares Bavli with Yerushalmi.
entries.annotation_md: - Uses Sefaria texts and links; includes optional AI notes generated with Gemini, which need checking.

entries.name: Sefaria Sidebar Extension
entries.summary: Chrome extension that shows a sidebar of Sefaria references on Daf Yomi sites for the daf being studied.
entries.annotation_md:
- Works on YUTorah, OUTorah, AllDaf, daf-yomi.com, E-Daf, Daf HaChaim, the Steinsaltz Center's English PDFs, RealClearDaf and Hadran.
- Published in the Chrome Web Store as the Talmud Sidebar Extension (next entry).

entries.name: Talmud Sidebar Extension
entries.summary: Chrome Web Store version of the sidebar that links a daf on other sites to its references on Sefaria.
entries.annotation_md: - The store listing names dafhachaim.org and daf-yomi.com as supported sites.
entries.status_note: Listing live 9-Oct-2026; last updated 18-Sep-2022, about 235 users.

entries.name: Stories of the Zohar: digital edition
entries.summary: Hebrew digital edition and database of the narrative passages of the Zohar, with search, comparison of stories, distant reading and motif browsing.
entries.annotation_md: - Sections for manuscripts and research bibliography; motifs include snakes, caves, the child, birds and encounters with strangers.

entries.name: Eitz HaRabanim
entries.summary: Interactive tree of more than 200 Talmudic sages showing teacher-student links, filterable by region and era.
entries.annotation_md:
- Filters for Eretz Yisrael and Babylonia and for Zugot, Tannaim and Amoraim; search in English or Hebrew.
- Data from Sefaria; [code on GitHub](https://github.com/ruebeckscube/talmud-family-tree).

entries.name: Sefer Similarity Map
entries.summary: Exploratory map that places books and chapters of Tanakh, Talmud and other texts by shared vocabulary, so related texts cluster together.
entries.annotation_md:
- Method: word and 2-4 word phrase counts, reduced to two dimensions with UMAP. The authors note it uses raw counts without tf-idf or lemmatization.
- Version 2.1.0 (2021).

entries.name: The Jewish Story Through Books
entries.summary: Animated map showing where and when Jewish books were written or published over the centuries.

entries.name: Liz Shayne: visualizations of Sefaria links
entries.summary: Blog post with network graphs of the roughly 87,000 links in the Sefaria library, made in Gephi.
entries.annotation_md:
- "Sefaria in Gephi: Seeing Links in Jewish Literature" (June 2014). An early example of network analysis on the corpus.
- [Code on GitHub](https://github.com/LizShayne/Sefaria-Data-Viz).

entries.name: HaMapah
entries.summary: Digital-humanities project that maps rabbinic responsa by place and time and analyzes their correspondence networks.
entries.annotation_md:
- Applies quantitative and geospatial methods to responsa metadata.
- Found via jewishai.me.
entries.status_note: Could not verify: the site returned HTTP 403 to an automated check on 9-Oct-2026.

entries.name: Jastrow App
entries.summary: Mobile-friendly, searchable Jastrow dictionary with a Hebrew keyboard, page navigation, abbreviation list and a timeline of sages.
entries.annotation_md: - Based on the 1903 printed edition; data from Sefaria. Also includes a guide to rabbinic time reckoning.

entries.name: Jastrow Search
entries.summary: Lightweight search page for quick lookup of Jastrow entries.

entries.name: Torah Tree
entries.summary: Hebrew collaborative wiki of Torah and halakha arranged as a tree on the model of the Rambam, with sources linked to the texts.
entries.annotation_md:
- Editors add and revise pages, with review before publication; discussion threads on pages.
- Built on Sefaria texts.
